subject: BlueAtlas SLA uplift & latency-credit proposal
messages:
From: Sofia Rodriguez <sofia@blueatlas.ai>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@blueatlas.ai
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA uplift request + credit mechanism

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the demo last week. BlueAtlas is excited about the throughput we saw in the PoC, but before we move to a 12-month commit we need stronger guarantees for production:

- Uptime target: 99.99% (we run customer-critical inference)
- Latency: p95 text-gen < 300ms for our typical 512-token requests
- Escalation: 24x7 oncall with a 30-minute initial response for Sev 1

We also want an explicit credit schedule if targets are missed (not a vague "credit at vendor discretion"). Please share a firm pricing delta for the 99.99% SLA (vs your standard 99.9%), any onboarding credits, and sample contract language.

Can you get me a proposal by next Tuesday (Aug 4)? We have procurement and legal lined up.

Regards,
Sofia Rodriguez
Head of Platform Engineering
BlueAtlas

Attachments: none

From: priyom.das@redwood.com
To: Sofia Rodriguez <sofia@blueatlas.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA uplift request + credit mechanism

Hi Sofia — thanks, and great to hear BlueAtlas wants to move forward. High level response below; I'm attaching a short pricing workbook and a draft SLA for your legal team.

Quick summary:
- Option A (Gold): 99.99% uptime, 24x7 escalation, 30-min initial response; expected uplift: +25% list over standard hosted pricing; credit schedule: 10% monthly credit banded by severity and frequency (see attached workbook).
- Option B (Silver): 99.95% uptime, business-hours escalation, 2-hour response; uplift: +12% list; smaller credits.

Two things I need from you to firm these numbers: monthly commit (tokens / qps) and expected peak QPS. If you can share usage profile (even a range) I'll lock numbers and populate the workbook.

I'm looping in Vanessa and Ben internally to check escalation capacity and the one-time onboarding credit we can offer for a 12-month commit.

Next steps:
1) You send a 30/90 day usage forecast
2) I'll return a redline-ready SLA + pricing workbook by Tue Aug 4

Regards,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing_workbook.xlsx, SLA_Draft_v3.pdf

From: priyom.das@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: BlueAtlas SLA uplift — concession request (internal)

Team — forwarding BlueAtlas. They want 99.99% + 30-min Sev1 response 24x7 and an explicit credit schedule. Preliminary thoughts below; reply with hard limits so I can close fast.

What I think we can offer without exec sign-off:
- 99.99% for hosted customers is possible if they commit to a minimum monthly spend (I was thinking $120k/mo equivalent).
- We can offer a one-time onboarding credit equal to 10% of first month usage (to offset migration cost) for a 12-month commit.
- Escalation: we can provide 24x7 triage + oncall retainer for P1s but anything beyond 2 hours of engineering intervention should be charged as “emergency engineering” unless we take a retainer.

Questions:
1) Ben — is there capacity risk to promise 30-min initial response for Sev1s across existing enterprise customers?
2) Rishi — can we structure the escalation retainer as a flat monthly (recommended $15k/mo) that reduces per-incident engineering fees?
3) Vanessa — any concerns on underwriting a 99.99% uptime for a new customer without dedicated pool?

Thanks — I want a crisp counter by EOD tomorrow so I can send BlueAtlas a firm offer.

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: priyom.das@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: BlueAtlas SLA uplift — concession request (internal)

Priyom / team — quick answers:

Ben: from ops perspective we can commit to 30-min initial acknowledgement for Sev1s if we do one of the following:
- BlueAtlas accepts a dedicated capacity pool (Dedicated offering) OR
- They agree to a $100k+/mo commit that allows us predictable slots and pre-warmed nodes.

Rishi: retainer is the right structure. Recommend: $12k/mo retainer with 8 hours/month included engineering time; overage billed at standard emergency rates. That retainer reduces our liability and preserves availability.

On 99.99% underwriting: I won't sign off on that uptime for hosted multitenant unless we have a hard commit (either Dedicated or the $100k/mo). If they want hosted without commit, we can offer 99.95% with the Silver uplift.

Concessions we can make to close: one-time onboarding credit = 10% of first-month committed spend; 3-month price hold on list rates for renewals; DocuSign-ready SLA with explicit credit table.

Ben — please confirm ops can support the dedicated pool ramp for onboarding timeline ~3 weeks.

-Vanessa
